chapters.html:
Mydei isn’t sure how to feel when Tribbie tells him the grim news.

First, in all honesty and completely disregarding Tribbie’s tearful expression, he takes it as a joke – Phainon, injured? Worse yet, cursed – can’t speak, see or hear? Such a tasteless prank. That would mean he lost to someone – someone who isn’t Mydei – or, at the very least, let his guard down enough to be in trouble. That’s unbelievable on its own, but… unless this is some sort of fucked up, terrible joke…

Mydei is to blame.

He was supposed to head out together with Phainon on a hunt, but they had a fallout the day before – one so stupid and unnecessary that he wonders how it escalated or why it even happened in the first place. It’s as normal as breathing for them to quarrel, but it’s the first time that Mydei felt the bitter taste of venom on his tongue.

The scene replays brokenly, blurrily in his mind – his fingers curling around the front of Phainon’s clothes to pull him close in anger; retribution in the form of a rebellious headbutt. He remembers the heat of their foreheads pressed together and the icy blue of Phainon’s eyes slanted in irritation; he remembers how low their voices went as they exchanged insults that got heavier and harsher.

In the end, Phainon pushed him out of his way and hissed “I can do this on my own” between gritted teeth, leaving immediately after.

Mydeimos let him.

If I were there with you—

“Lil’ De, please come with us,” the small redhead attempts, pulling him by the sash to gain his attention, “Snowy doesn’t let anyone touch him, or even get close. We’re so worried… we don’t know what to do…!”

He has so many questions. So many doubts and regrets, and so much anger about the whole situation.

The one thing he doesn’t have is hesitation.

He opens his eyes to see Phainon’s form, one knee on the ground and the other leg bent. His broadsword’s upright, the tip sunken into the earth and the handle gripped tightly by the Deliverer. He’s curled over himself beside the weapon with his head cast down, silver hair covering his face and lightly swaying with the chilly air floating around, a cold pocket dimension with its own atmosphere. Titankin corpses surround the immediate area, blood bathing the grass and turning it red.

Although Mydei has never seen Phainon in this particular stance, it’s easy to see that he’s on the defensive – seems ready to slay any danger that he may perceive as soon as it's within range.

“He’s attacking anyone and anything that approaches,” a feminine voice explains from behind him, confirming his first impressions.

The kremnoan spins on his heel to look at the ladies – Aglaea with a hand to her chest in a display of worry, and the redhead triplets huddled together holding hands. “Including you?” he directs at the blonde.

“Unfortunately. I believe Tribbie has briefed you on the situation, no? Phainon has been cursed,” she reaffirms, “He’s lost his sight, his hearing and his voice.”

“How did any of this happen?”

“We're looking into it. There's not much information at the moment,” the blonde says with a tinge of regret. “You may be able to help with the immediate situation, though.”

“Mmhm. What do I do? Knock him out?” the kremnoan suggests with a glance at Phainon, absentmindedly counting the cuts visible over his clothes. How’d he get hurt, this idiot? Mydei resists the temptation to curl his fingers into angry fists, if only to fool himself that it’s fine, this puppy-faced buffoon will be up and running in a moment.

“Nooo, poor Snowy!” and “Could you please be careful with him, Mydeimos?” are his simultaneous replies.

“I was joking,” he sighs, “I’ll try to be gentle.”

After all… I'm partially to blame.

He takes the first step towards Phainon. Considers whether to fight, to actually punch some sense back into the Deliverer’s face, or to simply defend himself when Phainon inevitably lunges at him – if there's one thing that man will recognize even if all of his senses are lost, after all, it's Mydei's strength.

Two more steps, and the chill begins to bite at his naked skin. Phainon’s stance changes. His grip on his sword tightens, head slowly lifting up to show vacant eyes staring ahead and a golden cut on his cheek. He looks tired. How long has he been on full alert, killing everything that comes close? Ever since he left yesterday?

“Look at you,” Mydei breathes out, his hot breath forming vapor, “You're a mess.”

Another step into the icy realm, and Phainon stands up. Broadsword in hand, he readies himself for the offensive – speckles of snow lift off the grassy ground, the air getting thick and heavy with an inebriating blend of power and fear – he's a cornered beast, ready to defend himself to the last breath. Mydei unbuckles his right gauntlet, sighing; a white cloud escapes from behind his teeth.

“I thought,” he teases, “You said you could handle this on your own?”

Phainon dashes towards him, sword cutting horizontally through the chilly air. Mydei stops the blade with his remaining gauntlet, sparks flying with the deafening clash; he holds it in place without allowing his feet to move even an inch. Phainon stops moving immediately, glazed eyes widening, lips parting.

They silently form Mydei’s name.

The kremnoan swallows down, a lump forming in his throat. “Get well soon so I can properly apologize for this fuck-up,” he murmurs, his gloveless hand lifting up towards Phainon’s face, “I don't want to owe you anything. I'm sure the opposite is also true.” Mydei's thumb draws over the cut on his icy cheek, and with every inch he crosses, the Deliverer further relaxes and his sword further descends, until he finally allows it to fall from his grasp.

He releases a shaky breath, eyelids fluttering closed as he loses his balance. Mydei quickly catches him by the waist, holding him upright, but there's no doubt that he's unconscious.

“Welp,” he grimaces, “Looks like I did knock him out.”

“He's stable… just tired, I suppose,” Aglaea affirms as she walks out of Phainon’s room, “But he will need to be cared for, for as long as this curse persists.”

Mydei makes a point of not looking at any of them, yet he feels all the eyes in the room right on his face, and hates what it means. At least the mood feels light enough that it reassures him things will be alright – an invisible weight lifts off his shoulders, and for that he is thankful. Alas:

“Sooo…” Tribbie begins, soundly smacking her lips.

“What a situation,” Aglaea laments.

“I wonder who will help him,” is Trinnon’s two cents.

“Now’s your cue, De,” Trianne whispers at him from in between her tiny hands, like it wasn't damn obvious his fate was sealed the moment they all looked at him.

“Splendid idea. Leave it to the homicidal maniac to be his caretaker; what could possibly go wrong?”

Aglaea smiles, either because she doesn't follow his logic or – most likely – because she doesn't care. Maybe she knows something he doesn't; he wouldn't put it past her to have understood all that happened the moment she went into that room. “If I remember correctly, you're the one who was able to calm him down.”

“If you don't remember correctly, we can barely stand each other on a good day.” He sighs, pressing a hand to his forehead. “In what world is this a smart move? If there's anything else I can do to help, like killing something, I’ll gladly—”

There's a loud noise from the bedroom, followed by glass breaking. Aglaea and the triplets run immediately inside, while Mydei hesitates for a second – bites his lip, clicks his tongue, rubs his face – not exactly out of annoyance, but because he knows he can snap that big idiot out of whatever trance he's in, and that annoys him.

He walks in just in time to see Phainon sitting on the ground right against the bed, the wounds on his naked upper body covered in bandages and an arm folded in front of his face, as if to protect it. There's a broken vase right beside him. His eyes are wide and searching for things that he unfortunately cannot see, chest moving rapidly with shallow breaths – it's impossible to tell what exactly he's thinking, but it's evident that he's anxious. Hopefully it's not a full-blown panic attack.

“Snowy…!” Tribbie whines, her sisters holding her small body as she trembles. Did he push her away?

“Let me try,” Mydei grumbles, crossing the distance between them to flick Phainon on the forehead. The startled Deliverer flinches, eyes widening just like last time, as he mouths Mydei's name. He’s always looked like a puppy, but this is just… unfair.

With hesitation, the kremnoan lands a hand over a tense, cold shoulder. In response, Phainon's breathing visibly slows down – he sighs, tiredly rubbing at his eyes, his body steadily relaxing. Crisis averted.

Mydei, of course, groans as loud as he possibly can without sounding like a dromas.

“You're not helping my case at all, damn it!”

“I imagine that means you will help,” Aglaea chuckles. “Rest assured – we will offer all the assistance you need, as well as search for a way to end this curse as soon as possible. Now, would you rather stay in his home, or bring him to yours?”

I wish I never had to see your face again.

Phainon curls himself further over his folded legs, face buried into his folded arms. Where is he…? He doesn't know. It feels like a bed, but could be a couch or a folded cloth on the floor for all he knows. At the very least, he's pretty sure his back is against a wall – feels hard and cold.

Mydei… Mydei took him somewhere. Home?

I don't want to talk to you anymore. I don't want to hear your stupid voice.

His lips quiver with a mix of anger, sadness, frustration, fear. He's trapped in his own body – a prison of absolute darkness and cold silence. He doesn't know what time it is, where he is, if he's alone or not, or what's happening beyond this cage of flesh he's caught in. He's living in a limbo.

This isn't at all what he wanted.

He'd been so angry, so furious – his fight with Mydei left him raging. In an uncharacteristically aggressive way to release stress, Phainon left by himself to hunt down and slay as many enemies as he could, all while those thoughts played in his head like a mantra, consuming his being.

I hate…

That last thought, he couldn't complete.

Tired and covered in blood, Phainon crouched down and hung his head between his legs with a sigh – I don't hate him, he'd thought. He's just angry. He's just stupid. They are stupid.

By the time he calmed down, though, it was already too late – the moment he stood up and opened his eyes, his world had lost its axis.

Biting down on his lip hard enough to taste blood, Phainon runs a hand through his hair and grabs it tightly. The universe itself is against him and his anger towards Mydei, it seems. Will he ever even go back to normal? Is this – whatever this is – even curable?

He releases his hair and realizes that he's trembling. Phainon places his hand in front of his face and flexes his fingers, closes and opens his fist, yet sees nothing but darkness. He barely feels real. Maybe he's dreaming, or caught in an actual limbo. Maybe he's dying. Maybe he's already dead—

There's a hot spark on his fingertip – warm, calloused flesh; an unmistakable, all-consuming heat. Mydei’s hand. Phainon’s breath catches on his throat as that warmth spreads from the tips of his fingers down to his palm, and encases his trembling limb.

He's suddenly very alive. The sharp contrast in temperature makes him dizzy, the convergence of their skins becomes the center of his universe, the intense grip stops his world from frantically spinning. Mydei’s hold slowly slides down towards Phainon's wrist…

…and makes him slap himself on the face.

“...son of a…!”

He snorts – unbelievable! – and, within moments and against all odds, begins to laugh. He doesn't hear the sounds he's producing, but feels the vibrations of the joyful sounds on his ribs and in his throat. His eyes feel wet. He wipes at them and collects many more tears than he'd rather have shed.

This isn't just mirth.

He's afraid.

“Mydei,” he calls out in complete silence into the void, “What have I done?”

Chapter Notes

Wowzers, thank you all SO MUCH for the feedback, holy shite!! ⸜(｡˃ ᵕ ˂ )⸝♡

I won't update this regularly as in... on a schedule, but I will update one or twice a week, so expect more updates soon! (˶˃ ᗜ ˂˶)

Mydei stands in the middle of the living room with arms crossed over his chest and a scowl. The next time anyone dares call him a psychopath, he's forcing them to take a look at Phainon's house.

He’s just finished taking a tour of the whole place – better get used to the plane of existence he's stuck in for the foreseeable future – and struggled to find just one disorganized item. This so-called ‘home’ is almost sterile.

In a way, he's thankful for that – albeit excessive a configuration, this means Phainon must know exactly where he keeps his things at all times. Mydei opted to stay at the Deliverer's house exactly to make his lack of sight easier on him, after all; he's going to need some level of independence if either of them mean to come out of this with their sanity intact.

Now that Mydei’s finished putting his things away in the guest room, he returns to the titular owner of the place – opens the door to Phainon's bedroom only to find him in the exact position as he'd left him some half an hour, forty minutes ago.

Phainon is, by no means, a small guy – he's not as tall as Mydei, of course; there's probably one third of an inch of height difference between them, really – and his clothes do hide meat and muscle alike, but… he looks tiny on his bed. Not only is the furniture large by itself, the way Phainon hugs his legs close to his chest and rest his chin on top makes him appear…

Mydei doesn't want to say vulnerable, but that's exactly what it is.

Phainon's blue gaze stares ahead, sometimes drifting off to one side or the other, but always vacant, completely lost. Reminds him of Aglaea, but he's aware the comparison isn't exactly fair and the Deliverer's natural puppy looks don't really help. It doesn't take much to see that he's absolutely miserable, and Mydei would pity him and his situation if it wasn't a disservice to his person.

He's considering messing with Phainon just to draw some sort of reaction when there's a knock at the front door – must be Tribbie; she did say she'd hop by after they were settled to check on them.

Mydei opens the door to find the gleeful redhead holding a big paper bag – “Pancakes!” she announces, “Lil's De’s favorites!”

“Lively, aren't we,” he greets as he's stepping away for her to enter. He leads her to the dining room and fishes through the cabinets – which one was it again? – for cutlery, making a mental note of where they are just so he isn't so lost the next time. After setting them on the table, he turns towards Phainon's room. “I’ll go get the snowflake.”

He briefly stands by the doorway – the Deliverer hasn't moved an inch. Unsurprising, yet still disappointing; Mydei hasn't lost hope that this curse will magically lift itself any moment now, after which he'll promptly solicit a duel so they can punch their apologies into each other's faces.

He decides to approach. Sitting close to the Deliverer, one leg bent on the bed, he's not surprised to have Phainon tense up and frown at his immediate direction, no doubt gauging whether he's a threat or not.

“It’s Mydei,” he attempts, “Tribbie brought some food.”

As expected, there's no response nor any sign that Phainon may have heard him. The only clue that he's even aware that there's someone close by is the tension in his body – it shows on his shoulders, on the strain in his expression, on the whitening of his knuckles as he holds his legs tight.

Mydei can't help the sigh that he releases. He reaches out for Phainon's hand, keeping his eyes on the Deliverer's expression as he allows his fingertips to glide over those strained knuckles. Phainon's breath visibly hitches, his Adam's apple bobbing with a gulp. He does relax, yet his blue irises soon dart away and his lower lip slips into his mouth – if he's embarrassed or just disgruntled, Mydei can't tell.

“You’re under the care of the goddamned crown prince of Kremnos, you know,” he murmurs with a smirk, “No safer place in the world. Maybe start being less suspicious of your surroundings?”

It's easy to imagine what kind of reply Phainon would give him – “I’d be safer pushing my head into a wasp’s nest” or some such nonsense… only to, indeed, heed to Mydei's words and calm down until the whole ordeal ended.

They're always dancing around each other like that, aren't they? Always teasing, but also trusting; pushing each other's buttons just enough to weave some sweet, positively delicious adrenaline into their interactions. To completely shift that pleasant dynamic into this… is simply torture.

“...we should get some food in your system before you starve,” Mydei ultimately mutters, sliding his hand to Phainon's wrist to pull on it, then guiding him into standing up. “If the last sound I’m able to hear from you is your stomach rumbling, I swear on Nikador’s name I will commit a crime.”

Phainon briefly loses his balance as he stands up, but quickly gathers himself. The kremnoan takes his hand to avoid more accidents and begins a slow stride, always looking back to make sure the Deliverer can accompany his pace, which he does… more or less. There's a look of utmost concentration on his face, his lips pressed into a thin line, and he's evidently trying his best to make his unsteady steps seem confident.

Tribbie’s already devouring her pancakes by the time they arrive back in the dining room; she stops at the sight of them, her cheeks full, big eyes slowly lowering towards their joined hands. Mydei refuses to comment on anything – the curious look on her face is very telling of her thoughts – and leads Phainon to the table. He sets the Deliverer's hand on the back of one of the chairs, allowing him to feel around it and to sit down at his own pace.

Mydei sits down himself, in front of the remaining one of three stacks of pancakes Tribbie set down, and looks up just in time to see Phainon sink his hand right into the slimy syrup over the dessert. The Deliverer grimaces, saying – no doubt – an incredibly dirty choice word that unfortunately they cannot hear, and lifts his hand up, fingers parting while the golden concoction drips down, and his eye twitching.

“Poor Snowy,” Tribbie pouts, “Maybe you should feed him, De!”

“Maybe I should eat all of these pancakes and leave none to you two.”

The redhead gasps and shoves a large piece into her mouth, chewing at the speed of sound. Mydei shakes his head with a small smile and turns his attention to the sticky situation with Phainon – takes his wrist, careful not to get any syrup on his own fingers, and makes the confused Deliverer taste the mess he's made of his hand.

Phainon is fast to catch on to the situation, and proceeds to lick himself clean. Mydei makes a face – I was going to hand you a napkin, stupid – but decides against commenting on anything. Tribbie finishes her pancakes right about the time he's about to begins eating his own, which leaves her with a lot of free time to talk, which he should have known is a terrible, terrible thing.

“You’re surprisingly apt at this,” she comments, beginning the countdown to the full destruction of Mydei's brain cells.

“I'm aware a certain someone calls me a troglodyte,” he grumbles, scowling pointedly at Phainon, who manages to find his fork and knife… but not to use them very well, “But I'm nowhere near a mindless killing machine. I do have empathy.” Sometimes.

“Well, we are talking about Snowy, so I guess you're right.”

Mydei stops moving with his fork halfway to his mouth, eyebrows nearly connecting with a frown. “I beg your pardon?”

“Nothing!”

Lies. Tribbie smiles big, elbows setting over the table and her little hands joining under chin. The kremnoan is almost tempted to press her for more but ultimately decides against it, instead briefly glancing at Phainon – his pancakes seem to have been ravaged by war, bits and pieces strewn around the plate. There's syrup on his nose.

Mydei wants to end the poor snowflake’s misery with a napkin to the face, but Tribbie keeps watching him, judging his every move , and it makes him mad. He'll just push Phainon under the shower once she leaves.

“Lil' De,” she calls in a curious tone, “You know you didn't have to say yes, right?”

He pauses again. Feels the last bit of his brain juices being squeezed right out of his head.

“You and Aglaea—”

“No one would be able to force you to do this if you didn't want to. You know there were other options, other Chrysos Heirs. You wanted this,” she interrupts with a smile, “You wanted to help Lil’ Phai.”

Phainon stabs his pancakes.

For a moment, Mydei actually thinks he heard the whole spiel and has his senses back, ready to attempt murder – good riddance! – but his hopes are crushed the moment he sees a piece of the dessert stuck to the Deliverer's cheek, frustration darkening his gaze.

“Wow. And they call me barbaric.”

“What can I say,” Tribbie shrugs with a teensy smile, getting up to leave and no doubt leave the pancake warzone for Mydei to take care of, “Peas in a pod!”

Mydei sighs.

Note to self: give Phainon a spoon next time.

It's an all-out attack on his remaining senses – the sweet smell of vanilla and caramelized sugar, the texture of what he guesses is pancakes on his tongue, the stickiness on his fingers and on his face. He can almost feel the particles dissolving in his mouth and sliding slowly down his cheek, and it's too much.

If he's managed to stab anything other than the table in frustration, he doesn't know. Part of him doesn't even care – he doesn't hear the sound of his knife hitting anything, but feels the impact reverberating up his palm and the tension taking hold of his jaw. His hands begin to tremble as he closes his eyes and counts to one, two, three, four, five…

He's halfway into an attempt to calm down when something soft touches his cheek – a tissue? Then, the next moment, there's something lightly pressing at his lips. He parts them – pancakes.

Oh, no.

Part of him wants to complain – his face certainly does, by burning up. Where is his dignity? Mydei, of all people, has to mouth-feed him, and Phainon can't quite decide whether that's the most terrible thing to have ever happened, or the best case scenario exactly because it's him. That guy will never bring this up in conversation. Ever.

At least the ridicule of the entire situation saves Phainon’s mind from that dark place for a while – maybe Mydei has the funniest grimace. Maybe he's mumbling-grumbling drivel like ‘the things I do for your snowflake ass' while actually wearing a smile.

His peace comes because of those thoughts, but also ends with them.

“Maybe,” he begins, lips opening and closing as he conjures up the right words, “I'll never see you again.”

It's distressing to feel the vibrations of the sounds he's trying to make, yet not hearing a single thing. He bites into his lower lip, refusing to let it tremble, and presses his hands together on his lap to attempt to achieve a similar effect.

“It's a pity, you know. I actually like it when you smile. Looks good… for a troglodyte,” he adds for good measure. Brings a small grin to his lips, like he hasn't lost control of every single thing, just… almost everything.

Unfortunately, he doesn't receive an equally petty response or a playful punch on the shoulder.

Eventually, Mydei guides him into standing up and leads him around the house – where are they? Phainon can't seem to grasp the layout. Maybe tomorrow… whenever tomorrow is, he can attempt to map out his surroundings, get a grasp of how to move in this state.

When they stop, despite knowing there's nothing to hear, he still attempts to concentrate to understand what he's supposed to be doing, if anything at all. A warm touch on his back makes his breath catch his throat, but it soon becomes a yelp – Mydei removes an adhesive right off his skin. Bandages? It does feel sore. There's a few more, too, on the shoulder, chest and stomach, and a small one on his cheek. Mydei seems to unroll one from his thigh, but it's over his pants; must've been an emergency patch-up.

Mydei takes his hand after a while and stretches his arm forward; Phainon flinches in surprise for a second upon feeling hot water.

Shower time. Got it.

Phainon removes his clothes and kicks them behind him, but he really can't shake off the invasive thought that alright, he's watching me shower, that's not awkward at all. It's not like they never went to the bathhouse together, right? Mydei's seen Phainon naked before. He even commented something along the lines of “wow, your butt is bigger than your brain” one time, which earned him a slap to his butt with Phainon's towel.

“Well, your dick is bigger than your brain and I really hope you don't take that as a compliment,” he says in belated retaliation.

Of course, his words don't make a single sound – perhaps for the best. Standing under the showerhead provides him relief, at least, from the sensory deprivation attempting to shred his lucidity. Mydei soon presses something cold and solid to his forehead – he takes it and feels around it, eventually finding a cap at the top. He flips it open and inhales the known scent of bergamots and chamomile. His body wash?

The familiarity of that smell – and also of probability of being in his house, or so he hopes – puts his mind more at ease. He washes his hair first, feeling around the cold tiled wall until he finds yes, that's my setup! and places down the bottle he's holding so that he can free his hands.

It's like he's having this experience for the first time in his life – Phainon feels every element of the foam and bubbles forming around his fingertips and sliding down his skin, the slickness of his wet hair tickling his palm, inhales that sweet herbal scent like its source is right under his nose. It's intense.

Even the water itself feels different – it massages his scalp and shoulders with the pressure from the shower, but runs down his body in heavy, hot trails that contour his frame.

He releases a heavy, deep sigh and lifts up his head, hands moving to his neck to explore his own skin. It raises goosebumps down his arms, his gut flipping upside down. He concentrates on the sensation, fingertips sliding up towards his scalp, behind his ear, down his cheeks and his lips. He allows his hands to move down his chest and stomach, following his own curves, tracing his hip bones.

He's alive. He's really alive, and the only way he can feel it is through his skin, through the scents filling up his lungs.

It's impossible to tell whether Mydei's watching him or not, but eventually the kremnoan does turn off the shower. He drapes a towel over Phainon's head and leads him somewhere else, possibly the bedroom. He only confirms that when Mydei guides him into sitting on the bed, towel falling to his lap.

He disappears for a while. If he's getting clothes or something else, Phainon doesn't know.

A moment later a weight settles behind him on the mattress, and he's confused until the wounds on his back begin to burn – antiseptics, no doubt. He sucks his lower lip into his mouth and frowns until the terrible sensation ends, only to be replaced by the soothing warmth of Mydei's hand pressing fresh bandages to his skin. He repeats the same over each and every wound Phainon has, moving to the other side of the bed to bandage his chest, his shoulder, his cheek.

The injury on his thigh is the one that hurts the most. Phainon grimaces, eyebrows darting together and a silent groan escaping him. Mydei seems to notice his discomfort, because he slows down and even allows his touch to linger. It's soothing. Phainon releases a shaky breath, tired of everything, and leans back until his body hits the mattress.

Mydei's touch disappears and he almost regrets having laid down.

The towel’s pulled away from his lap, causing him to yell out – “Mydeimos!” – in surprise; that was the only thing shielding his privacy. “You're not even taking me out for dinner first?” he laughs, “Rude!”

He half expects Mydei to jab back at him with his sharp tongue, but remembers there's no possible communication between them. It's possible they'll never banter again, never exchange a good laugh after a glass of alcohol loosens them up enough to be openly friendly. He may not see Mydei and his too-good-for-a-troglodyte smile anymore, and these were already rare to begin with. There's also all the things that are not Mydei that he may forever miss out on, but just considering thinking about those makes him exhausted.

The duvet is soon draped over his body, which he guesses ends this bout of interaction, and what little hints of contentment he had managed to gather quickly dissipate.

“Mydei,” he murmurs weakly, pressure building inside his chest and behind his eyelids, “I’m not okay.”

His silent admission goes unanswered.

Chapter End Notes

I know what you're thinking and no, Mydei didn't peek. He is a gentleman. (⁠´⁠⊙⁠ω⁠⊙⁠`⁠)⁠！

chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

Guess who hasn't completed the 3.0 quest yet? *cries in moms don't have much free time* I really hope I haven't been butchering their personalities too much! I'm making an effort I SWEAR

Out of absolutely nowhere, there's a bump.

Mydei opens his eyes – fuck, they're sore. It's still dark out. Silence. His eyelids slide right back down.

Badonkadonk.

He turns around on the bed, forcing his eyes to stay open and stare at the ceiling while straining his ears to listen some more. Silence. He glances at the clock on the wall – fifteen past three in the morning. His jaw pops with a yawn, eyes watering up with the tempting sleepiness washing at them. He closes them once more.

Bump— crack. Clatter.

Mydei sits up with his body tingling from sleep, eyes nearly crossing from lack of control. Bad cycle to wake up from, he muses. He throws his legs off the bed, getting up with yet another yawn and both hands rubbing at his face to try and stay awake. He doesn't sense any danger, so what in the nine layers of hell could be making all this ruckus?

It's difficult to navigate the unfamiliar house in the dark, especially when his eyes really want to stay closed, but he manages. Scratching his tummy, he turns a corner—

—to see Phainon, completely naked – perhaps it’s best to offer him clothes after he's done showering next time – crouched in the middle of the living room, trying to pick up who knows what from the ground.

“Phainon,” he calls out with hope, “Do you have any idea what time it is? It's fuck-you o’clock. Go back to bed.”

Of course, no response. Well, an attempt was made – sighing, Mydei looks around for the light switch and turns it on, spewing a few incoherent curses at the sudden glare before looking at his protegee once more.

He's currently picking pieces of a broken flower vase from the floor; seems he knocked it out of the coffee table. Mydei curiously approaches, but hurries in his steps once he realizes just how perilous that activity is – in order to find the broken pieces, Phainon keeps sliding his hand around the floor and getting it caught on the jagged edges.

“Seriously?! Why wouldn't you just leave this to me?!” the kremnoan barks as he crouches in front of Phainon, taking his wrists to make him stop. The Deliverer glances at his direction but makes no attempt to release the shards he's already holding. Mydei has to actually take them from him and place them on the table.

Returning his attention to Phainon's hand, Mydei grimaces at the many small cuts he acquired, specks of liquid gold and humid dirt all throughout. “You’re bleeding,” he whispers out loud, more to himself than anything. If Phainon didn't look so unhappy, the kremnoan would absolutely smack him across the head for dealing with harmful things on his own in his vulnerable state.

“You may be an idiot for doing this, but I suppose I understand where you're coming from,” he says as he's guiding Phainon into standing up, “I would want to do as many things on my own as I possibly could if I were in your place. There is a limit to everything, though, like this right here. Dumbass.”

Careful not to step on the shards or to cause Phainon to do it, he leads them back to the main bedroom and towards the bed. He leaves the Deliverer there, his back to the headboard, to get the first aid kit one more time.

He sits across from Phainon — “You know what, let's not keep your broadsword out in the open,” he grumbles while taking a pillow and placing it on the Deliverer's lap – and takes out wet tissues and disinfectant to begin tending to his wounds. It's all small cuts, thankfully, but unfortunately these tend to sting the most – Phainon tries to suppress a grimace but, as far as Mydei's concerned, he's failing terribly.

“Hurts like a bitch, eh?”

He wonders how Phainon would reply. Probably something like “well you're a bitch”, with a lopsided smirk that makes it look like he thinks his remark was terribly intelligent.

Before he ends up creating an entire fictional conversation between them in his head, Mydei forces his focus to return to Phainon's hands. Now that the adrenaline’s going down, he's starting to get sleepy again – better finish before he falls asleep on the job.

He eventually places the last bandage around Phainon's pinky finger, and it's right then that he's overtaken by his biggest, longest yawn yet. It leaves him paralyzed for a moment, eyes watering up and jaw locking open until he's done – but by then, he's awoken all over again.

Phainon's touching his chest.

It's just his fingertips, feeling around so softly it almost tickles, slowly gliding down his sternum towards his stomach. Mydei quirks an eyebrow and keeps watching, allowing whatever experiment Phainon's attempting out of curiosity, if nothing else.

That seems to be the Deliverer's reason, too – his touch is almost timid, apologetic, his hand retreating when he reaches Mydei's navel. His lips move like he's saying something, eyes glancing away and the blue within them quivering. An apology, maybe? No way to pry. Instead, Mydei takes a hold of Phainon's hand and splays it on the center of his chest, over his heart.

The Deliverer stays unmoving for a moment, a look of either surprise or disbelief on his face, even after Mydei removes his own hand to allow him to roam free. After a moment he presses his palm more firmly, likely feeling the kremnoan’s heartbeats after receiving this half-permission, half-invitation. His touch steadily rises towards Mydei's clavicle and Phainon's other hand joins – he traces the length of the bone with his fingertips, hands splaying at the shoulders and moving slowly back to the chest.

They move up once more, never breaking off contact, instead following every curve on the path to Mydei's neck, fingers tickling the nape with a soft touch and briefly catching on his hair. He follows the angle of the kremnoan's jaw, traces his ears little by little, accompanies the arc of his cheekbones and the bridge of his nose.

Phainon is a cartographer mapping out uncharted territory, Mydei muses. He's fully concentrated, as if committing everything to memory with as most accuracy as humanly possible. His hands are large and calloused and the edges of the bandages on his fingers are choppy, but his touch is still warm and careful, gentle even, the heat of his palms pressing into Mydei's cheeks as he cups them both.

That serious look on his face softens for a moment, as if he's found a little treasure – he gives a few squeezes as if Mydei’s cheeks are squeaky toys and chuckles, chest moving with every sound that doesn't come out, eyes slanting to follow the happy curve of his pink lips. Pretty. His mouth moves like he's saying something; Mydei can't translate the sound of silence, yet it makes his face feel warm and his ribcage crammed.

He draws breath from behind closed teeth, an attempt to rewire his brain back from the idiotic, amused mush it’s apparently turned into. “The nerve of you to treat a prince as a toy,” he grumbles without bite, if only to distract himself from how charming Phainon’s innocent curiosity and glee are. They only increase when the Deliverer realizes he can feel Mydei talking to him by the movements of his jaw. He seems to find that interesting so Mydei then adds to the fake intimidation, knowing his actual words can’t be heard but that the grinning puppy across from him knows him well enough to understand him by proxy: “I am not your plaything, Snowflake. Just you w— hnnph?! Mmh!”

Alright, so apparently Mydei can’t speak with a bunch of fingers shoved into his mouth.

Phainon retrieves his hand before the kremnoan makes him, but it’s only to place it on his stomach as it convulses with laughter. Mydei wants to be angry at him, but finds that it’s impossible – he’s overtaken by an indignant, lopsided smirk. “You menace,” he breathes out. At least his apparent archenemy Phainon the Terrible is unable to hear the mirth in his voice.

To the kremnoan's chagrin, though, the exploration of his face isn’t over yet – Phainon reaches for his lips. Traces every inch of them with his thumb even slower than he'd been moving before, applying pressure to part them, humidifying them with saliva. Mydei feels lightheaded. Maybe he's stopped breathing. Can't tell. Phainon, on the other hand, simply looks enchanted and absolutely satisfied with the sheer torture he's inflicting, happy even.

Mydei retaliates by biting Phainon's finger.

The Deliverer seems to yelp in surprise, but ultimately chuckles at the attack. He removes his hands from Mydei's face only to slide them up his scalp, fingers weaving around his hair and sliding down the strawberry blonde locks. He tries to talk again, lips moving without producing sound, and the kremnoan can only imagine what he's saying. Perhaps it's something about lion manes, just like the first time he touched Mydei's hair.

They’d been less sober then, relaxing in the baths together. Mydei had his back to the walls of the pool, arms behind him, while Phainon was the opposite – was sitting sideways, chest to the wall and arms folded above them. Mydei distinctly remembers what a challenge it was not to stare at the sharp curve of Phainon's naked waist. When the Deliverer reached out to touch his hair, though, it became impossible not to stare – either at the shiny water running down the skin of his broad shoulders, at the drunken pink dust on his cheeks, or at the way his tongue followed the path of his smiling lips and left them glossy and red. He’d then tucked a few locks of Mydei's hair behind his ear.

“Just like a little lion’s mane,” he’d murmured.

His gut flips upside down and Mydei promptly decides that's enough touching for the night. He takes Phainon by the wrists to take them off him, and only realizes how rough he was when the poor thing flinches. He immediately softens his grip, but judging from how the joy fades from Phainon's face, the damage has long been done. “I’m sorry,” he whispers genuinely, despite knowing his apologies won't be heard, “I was careless.”

In an attempt to explain away his unfortunate reaction in a way the other will understand, Mydei swallows down his pride and places Phainon's hand over his racing heart. Though the Deliverer stays still as if processing the information and the slightest rosy tint befalls his cheeks and the tips of his ears, it's hard to know whether he's been forgiven or not, especially since Phainon looks away and doesn't even attempt to say a thing.

Mydei ultimately releases him, a tired sigh pushing out of his ribs. Hopefully his actions haven’t irreversibly hurt the trust Phainon has in him and they'll both forget about this by the time morning rolls around.

It seems to be getting steadily easier to recollect himself each time he wakes up from slumber – the confusion until Phainon remembers his current situation and adjusts to it has been diminishing, and the sense of dread keeping him bound in place, like his veins are filled with liquid lead, is slowly vanishing. That’s good, he thinks.

He still can’t get out of bed.

It took him a while to fall back asleep after what happened – feels like he terribly fucked up. He enjoys tormenting Mydei, yes, and provoking him to elicit entertaining responses, but it’s never been his intent to make the man uncomfortable. Makes him second-guess that interaction from the very beginning – was Mydei feeling uneasy then?

What did it mean that Mydei's heart was racing? Was he anxious? Happy? Embarrassed, nervous, excited? That gesture didn't answer any questions more than it raised them.

Phainon presses the heels of his palms to his eyes until it begins to sting and takes a breath deep enough to strain his lungs. Once he’s sufficiently diminished the storm brewing inside his chest, he decides that the only way he can make up for what happened is becoming independent enough that Mydei won’t have to babysit him anymore.

He actually started doing that the last time he got up – wanted to move around the house and get an idea how to locate himself and the things around him, but all he did was bump into every possible piece of furniture he could and break what he’s sure is – was – his favorite flower vase. Well, he’s not too disheartened yet… in fact, he’s even more intent on doing things right and getting used to this hopefully temporary ailment.

The difference is that before, he wanted to map out the house just so he wouldn’t be entirely dependent on Mydei and to feel more like himself rather than a statue, and now… he wants, needs complete autonomy.

He psychs himself up – no bumping into shit this time – and gets off the bed only to become completely disoriented. He attempts to make a rendering of his bedroom in his head, but it's difficult gauging the distance between everything and even knowing the direction he's really facing when he's so used to relying on his sight.

Of course, the first thing he does is bumping his knee into the nightstand. At least that helps with his orientation… kind of.

The first order of business is finding his clothes. He attempted to do that the last time too, but ended up finding the door instead and left to walk around the rest of the house, but he's not losing his focus now – his privates have been freshened enough that they're practically brand new; he needs some underwear pronto.

He repeats the route he took in his last attempt, tiny step by tiny step, but instead of going through the door he continues adjacent to the wall until he hits his wardrobe. “See, wasn't so difficult,” he tells himself with a small smile. Now he just has to feel around every handle until he thinks he has the right one and finds his underwear drawer.

It takes him about half of an eternity, but he's still proud of himself when he manages to fully dress up – a shirt, underwear and pants… even if he had to sit on the floor to be able to put on the last two items. He retraces his steps towards the door and moves out, unable to rely on any walls to reach the kitchen for a most needed glass of water because of all the free space he now finds himself with.

Now that he's out of the sanctuary of his room, he doesn't allow himself to look weak and worried. Instead of tiny steps, he takes confident strides – though with his arms outstretched, hands at the ready to serve as the first point of contact – even when he has no idea where he's going.

“Kitchen, a-kitchen, I wanna find my kitchen,” he singsongs, just to deescalate the stress building up inside him. His limbs feel rigid, his core shaking, every inch tread into the unknown further accelerating his heartbeats. He finally comes upon something, extended palms hitting something soft and warm—

—like flesh.

His breath catches up in his throat and it's painful, thorns rather than oxygen. He immediately retreats, moving away – maybe backwards; he doesn't know, he's moving somewhere – but his lower back meets something cold and stiff – the kitchen counter? – while cold sweat forms on the back of his neck.

“Mydei—”

Before he can even formulate his next words, the kremnoan pulls him into his chest, arms firm around his waist. His nose blows hot air next to Phainon's ear and at his hair, causing the locks to tickle his skin; the effect is intensified when he whispers something, perhaps a small nothing right into his ear. It melts him. Melts his core, melts his structure, melts his all when one of Mydei's hands slide up towards his scalp and presses him closer.

He hadn't noticed how harshly his heart had been thundering until it began to calm down – until he breaks free of his hesitation and slowly embraces Mydei back, arms locked around his neck and his face burying within. He draws in a shaky breath – smells warm, like the sun and melted sugar and spiced cider. Like safety.

“...I didn't fuck up at all, did I?”

Though Phainon receives no verbal response, the warm feeling buzzing in his chest replies with a soundly no, we're okay.

“We're okay,” he breathes out with a smile.

Chapter Notes

As usual -- holy shit?? You've all been so nice to me and this story! It makes me genuinely happy. And, GOOD NEWS! I now have a beta reader!! ฅ^>⩊<^ ฅ Kourt has been helping me out and she's AMAZING. Check out her

With his immediate worries laid to rest, Phainon finds himself chuckling into the crook of Mydei's neck, soft hair locks tickling his nose. “I can't wait to ask you to hug me again when this is over,” he says with humor, “I'll tease you so much you'll want to kill me.”

Mydei will have even more reasons to tease him rather than the other way around, but Phainon will make that sacrifice – he's always known that the gruffy prince had a softer and caring side, but had no idea he could be this sweet.

One time, he saw Mydei scolding one of his men in the middle of the city and, intending to deescalate the situation if necessary, Phainon approached. He was about to greet the two when he head Mydei spout a stern, “No. You will go home and rest.”

“But sir–”

“Do you want to anger me?”

“That’s not very difficult to do,” Phainon intervened, stopping beside them. The man Mydei was talking to, however, seemed to have already made his mind – while the prince threw Phainon a nasty, annoyed look, the downcrest soldier simply nodded and left.

“...what happened to him? He doesn't look so good.”

“That's exactly why I'm telling his stubborn ass to rest,” the kremnoan explained with a sigh. As if Phainon wasn't there – or perhaps, knowing the Deliverer wouldn't simply leave – he started to walk away.

“I wonder how long this lost puppy will follow me,” he eventually said. Of course Phainon gave him the only plausible response – an enthusiastic bark – and pretended not to see Mydei’s little smile as they walked through Okhema.

Their itinerary seemed so mundane. Phainon genuinely didn't connect two and two together when they bought a plethora of fruits, vegetables and juices, and continued on in an unfamiliar route. They reached a house that was not Mydei's, as far as Phainon knew, and knocked on the door. When a woman with beautiful chocolate hair and the greenest eyes opened the door, Phainon caught himself staring agape at the still very serious prince beside him.

“Sick people need to eat and rest properly,” Mydei told the woman as he pushed the groceries into her arms, “Don't let that idiot push himself too hard.”

She was surprised for a moment, but quickly recomposed herself with a beaming smile. “Oh, thank you! I'll let him know you sent your regards!”

After all was said and done, Phainon turned to Mydei and asked the question that had been eating at him, to the point of nearly hollowing him out inside – “So she's not your…?”

Mydei smirked in response, and Phainon's face heated up before the kremnoan could even begin to speak – “No. Were you jealous?” was the heresy he chose.

Phainon answered with his fist.

There were also small things that Mydei did when he thought no one was looking – one day, Phainon caught him freeing a spider out the window of his house. They both stopped moving, eyes wide at each other, Phainon's gaze switching between the arachnid on the windowsill and the angry half naked man with bed hair behind it.

“...what are you doing?” Phainon finally asked.

“No, what are you doing?”

“Watching you help a spider, apparently?”

“I'm not helping the spider; I'm just—”

“You're helping the spider.”

“And you're trespassing!” the kremnoan barked with his cheeks flaring red, fingers moving through his messy hair to, no doubt, fail at attempting to make it presentable. “Why in the nine hells are you in my backyard when I have a perfectly functional front door?!”

“...I heard those pancakes you like are on sale,” was Phainon's way of inviting Mydei for breakfast and to divert the kremnoan's attention from the fact that he's committing a crime. Before they left for their meal – and the promise of throwing hands later on – Mydei briefly excused himself and went to his small, surprisingly well kept – and walled – backyard.

Phainon had a hunch what the kremnoan was doing. Upon his return, the Deliverer smiled innocently – “Was your little friend alright?”

“...I will punch a new hole into your face.”

For weeks after that, Phainon would ask if Arachnysius – the name he gave the spider without Mydei's permission – was doing well and, to his surprise, the kremnoan had a different tale to tell every time… including admitting to offering it the occasional mosquito as a sacrifice, “to make an example for the others.”

There's even more tiny acts of kindness that he's witnessed, so yes, he knew all along that Mydei isn't half the heartless bastard he portrays himself as… he just never thought he'd ever have that soft side directed at him.

Mydei couldn't have been forced to do this, right? Phainon wouldn't call them friends exactly, but their hostility towards each other has no vitriol – he would say it's actually very sportsman-like.

However, Phainon considers being very, very hostile when Mydei attempts to part from him.

Since he's unable to voice out his indignation, Phainon settles with closing his grip around the kremnoan's neck tighter than a starving snake around a hefty snack. Mydei's voice vibrates from inside his chest into Phainon's own, maybe some sort of complaint or a request for him to calm down. He answers by not moving an inch.

Then he moves a lot of inches.

His world loses its axis so suddenly he's left short winded – Mydei hoists him up with ease, hot hands firm on the back of his thighs, their hips flush against one another. Despite his current deafness, Phainon swears he hears the sound of his own heartbeats inside his ears, and the rush of blood to his face.

He loses the breath he barely even had when Mydei lets him down on the kitchen counter he'd been leaning against, fingers immediately finding the Deliverer's stomach and tugging on his shirt.

Phainon chokes.

‘Undress’ is the command hidden within Mydei's gestures. It's impossible to stop the surge of heat flaring up in Phainon's gut; he attempts to close his legs, but Mydei's right between them. The pressure against his inner thighs makes him lightheaded.

Another tug on his shirt. Phainon gathers just enough of his liquid brain that he's able to send his arms the instruction to take off the apparently offending fabric before Mydei decides to rip it to shreds. It tickles his skin on the way out, leaving it prickly and sensitive, as if there's micro-bolts of electricity zapping through his capillaries. Of all the unholy things running through his mind, the one that sticks out the most is, infuriatingly, I think my nipples are hard. Does he know that my nipples are hard? I think I'm dying. I'm definitely dying. May the Gods have my soul.

Mydei takes the shirt from his hands. There's a small breeze that briefly kisses Phainon’s heaving chest, as if the kremnoan is moving, and… the collar of the fabric goes right back through his head.

He's mortified. Petrified. Embarrassified. Would bury a hole into the ground and jump right in if he could. He would welcome the apocalypse instead of fighting against it if he had just one more screw loose.

I must've worn it inside out, he belatedly realizes.

The sudden drop in adrenaline makes him release that one choked breath clogging his throat. “Unbelievable,” he grumbles, sliding his arms into the short sleeves, “Is this revenge for the spider thing?”

Since he's unable to hear what the absolute pest has to say about that, he decides that yes, Mydei was positively, mind-numbingly erotic because Phainon teased him for befriending a spider. That makes sense.

The thing that – surprisingly – disappoints him the most about the whole thing, though, is that Mydei's intentions weren't as immoral as Phainon's thoughts. Nothing was done with the intent of being sensual – that's just how the Deliverer's stupid senses perceived the whole thing. If only—

His thoughts are rudely interrupted by something round, small and cool pressing against his lips. Phainon frowns out of spite but still opens his mouth to accept Mydei's offering – a grape, firm on the outside, but tender and as sweet as honey inside.

Just like him.

It's the seventh time he reads this paragraph without absorbing a single word. He counted.

It's not that he's very invested in this book – it's some sort of generic fictional tale with heroes and monsters that he found on Phainon's shelf – but he would like the distraction. All he can think about is why is this happening?

The shallow, summarized version of the answer is, of course, Phainon didn't want to let go of him.

He's just not sure how that translated into moving around the house with the Deliverer clinging to his neck with the angriest puppy face he's ever seen, and then culminated in Mydei laying down on the sofa to read with Phainon resting on top of him; seems to have fallen asleep a while ago. He's even using Mydei's chest as a pillow like it's the most natural thing in the world.

Maybe it is.

Mydei feels strangely… ordinary, and not in a bad way. It's like he's a normal person with a normal life, and not a demigod prince with blood and death in his hands. It's a separate world within these walls – slow and peaceful, bright and warm as if the sun is constantly cradling them.

He gives up on reading entirely – leaves the book on the backrest and allows his eyelids to slide closed, fingertips lightly tapping a melody without rhythm into Phainon's ribs. He wouldn't mind sleeping like this at night. It could actually be very useful to signal to the Deliverer that it's nighttime, and that he shouldn't go around knocking random vases off furniture.

Would Phainon share his bed with him? Probably. He's been so clingy, it's almost sad – he must be relying a lot on his sense of touch to stay sane, and —

And Mydei is the only one around.

He opens his eyes. Stares at the ceiling. There's a pit forming in his stomach.

It's not difficult to imagine Phainon in this situation with someone else – who doesn't like this charismatic puppy? He seems like he doesn't dislike many people either. It's easy to picture a pair of feminine, gentle hands carding through Phainon's hair and his smile in return; easy to picture him laying on another person's chest.

He stops tapping on the Deliverer’s ribs.

Tribbie… may have been right. Maybe Mydei did want to do this. If you want a job well done, do it yourself, no? But they never asked for Phainon's opinion; couldn't. Would he prefer to have someone else care for him? Someone with more tact, more gentleness, more patience? Someone that simply isn't Mydei?

The answer is so crystal clear that it makes him sigh in frustration. He pinches the bridge of his nose and tries to will away the discomfort in his gut, but it doesn't work. His blood feels like it's running cold – I shouldn't be here, his brain plays on repeat. It's deafening.

It takes him a moment to notice that Phainon’s awakening – slowly sits up on Mydei's lap, one hand on the kremnoan's abdomen for support while the other rubs at his eyes, a silent yawn briefly contorting his features. He blankly looks around, eyes still lacking focus but ultimately stopping in the direction of Mydei's chest.

Phainon seems to say his name. His hands blindly roam over Mydei's torso towards his neck, then find his face just like he'd done the night before, hands pressing heat into his skin.

He's smiling. Looks absolutely angelic – snow white hair crossing the blues of his eyes and casting shadows over his cheeks, his curved lips the faintest peachy-pink. They move as he says something else, allowing a small peek at his rosy, glistening tongue.

A discomforting flush of heat burns the nape of Mydei's neck, the tips of his ears and his cheeks. He sits up intent on leaving, trembling hands on Phainon's arms – and remembers himself committing the same mistake just the night before.

Phainon waits, quietly, for his rejection. It shows in his eyes and in the way his smile fades. He seems anxious. Mydei breathes, but it isn't enough. I'm sorry, he’d said the night before, I was careless.

Fighting against his impulse to leave, Mydei instead mimics Phainon's gesture and hesitantly cups his boyish cheeks, enticing a look of surprise. His skin is so soft it tickles Mydei's calloused hands, and his face fits so well in his palms that it's difficult to want to let go.

“You're feeling more confident now, aren't you? Moving around the house,” Mydei murmurs, fingers moving towards Phainon's scalp, “Dressing up on your own. Being stubborn.”

The Deliverer seems to melt under his touch – closes his eyes and relaxes, a small smile returning in tandem with a chuckle, his cheeks and the tip of his nose flushing a healthy pink. Mydei’s heart skips a beat; he orders it to behave.

“...maybe you don't need me specifically anymore. You just need to not be alone.”

Perhaps it's best that Phainon can't hear him – he would definitely notice the lack of conviction in Mydei's voice.

“I'll talk to Aglaea,” Mydei ultimately whispers, “We'll find someone more suitable to be your caretaker.”

Mydei keeps glancing at the clock on the wall – “Give me a couple hours and I'll be there,” Aglaea told him. He sighs and returns his attention to the pan he's holding, chopped vegetables turning an appetizing golden. It smells nice and he knows the taste will be satisfactory, yet he has no appetite.

Phainon's on the table behind him, drinking juice and feeling around the table for things to mess with. He almost tipped his glass over twice already, shoved his hand into a sugar container, smeared whipped egg whites all over his face and fell back on his chair when attempting to balance on it. He had the guts to laugh about it while a worried Mydei felt around for any cracks on his thick fucking skull.

Honestly, he hoped that those many shenanigans would make him angry, that he'd lose his patience or that he'd feel anything negative that would make parting ways easier but… to his chagrin, everything Phainon does has the opposite effect: it’s all too endearing.

When the food is done, Mydei sits beside him and offers him a plate, guiding his hand to the spoon on the side. Phainon finds the edge of the plate with his free hand and seems to use some mental measurement to find where to dip the spoon – he succeeds, despite some vegetables falling down, and takes the first mouthful.

His cheeks puff out as he's eating, eyebrows rising on his forehead – he seems pleased. There's a small smile playing by his lips as he carries on eating, though he does show occasional irritation when failing to capture anything with the spoon and it reaches his mouth completely empty. Before the annoyed puppy ends up deciding to go for violence, Mydei takes the cutlery from him and feeds him himself.

Phainon happily eats everything. Once full, he swats the air until his hand lands on Mydei's shoulder and follows a trail up towards his face. He won't miss me, as the Deliverer stops moving altogether, chest rising and falling quickly.

He'll get used to being touched by another person. He'll lean on them for support, map out their face with his calloused fingers and take naps on their lap. He'll hold their hand like it's an anchor keeping him at bay, show them his vulnerable side, give them that smile that makes Mydei feel dumb. Maybe they'll feel dumb too.

Maybe.

Maybe Phainon will look for Mydei later. Maybe he'll be disappointed not to find him. Maybe he'll miss eating Mydei's food. Maybe he'll think he's being rejected again, that Mydei abandoned him, that he did something wrong. That he's a burden. That Mydei didn't want him.

Just maybe.

Aglaea gasps – Phainon’s snatched his hand away from her and begins moving around, swatting blindly at the air. His chest quickly rises and falls, breath visibly shallow, eyes darting everywhere in distress.

If she replies, he doesn't hear it. Doesn't care – he'll apologize later for wasting her precious time. The only thing that matters right now is Phainon embracing him back, fingernails digging into the skin of his back hard enough to burn, a shaky sigh blowing at the nape of his neck.

“I'm sorry,” he whispers, “For being selfish like this.”

Whatever the hell happened, it's over. Phainon won't try to make sense of things out of his reach; he has enough problems to deal with and there's no way he's adding to that of his own volition. He can question Mydei later, or at least he hopes he will be able to.

The kremnoan eventually parts from the hug and leads him to the shower, helps him brush his teeth and offers him a fresh set of clothes after he's done. To Phainon's surprise, Mydei even dries his hair with the towel and combs it for him as he's sitting on the bed. “Heh, feeling like pampering me today?” he inquires. “Too bad we can't talk. I miss making you annoyed on purpose.”

Phainon’s body feels heavy. He lies down, the mattress plump, the sheets soft and cool against his skin, the pillow a cloud of comfort beneath his head.

“I miss a lot of things about you,” he admits. “Did you know you avoid eye contact when you're lying? And your ears blush when you're embarrassed. I think it's cute.” He chuckles low, tired. “You'd punch my teeth in if you knew I find anything about you cute.”

There's weight on the bed beside him. Mydei's fingers card through his hair, nails grazing at his scalp – heavenly. Phainon closes his eyes and turns around on his side, facing the kremnoan's direction.

“Your hair looks like it's on fire when the sunset hits it just right,” he continues, “And your eyes crinkle when you smile. Your voice drops an octave when you're sleepy – sounds nice. I like your voice.”

A yawn interrupts his thoughts. He curls over himself, Mydei's fingers continuing their holy work on his scalp.

“And you're not nearly as discreet as you believe,” he smiles, “I know you look at me when you think I'm not paying attention. I never told you because I don't want you to stop.”

The mattress shifts – Mydei must be getting up. He drops the duvet over Phainon's body; the Deliverer sighs in defeat – time to sleep, it seems.

“Maybe I'll tell you someday,” he quietly whispers, “How you make me feel alive.”

For now, all he can do is catch some shuteye—

Mydei settles beside him again, shifting around, moving the duvet to, what, cover himself up too? The fuck's going on? Is Mydei actually staying? Phainon doesn't protest in any way, shape or form – doesn't even move just to make sure he won't scare the kremnoan away.

After a while, though, he can't help but seek the comfort of Mydei's warmth – slowly but steadily, his hand moves over the bed in a hesitant search. His fingertips find a source of heat and softly feel around it, discovering Mydei's own fingers. He cautiously entwines their pinkies, and it's such a silly and childish motion it makes him blush – he feels the hotness creeping up his face like a lava riptide, but doesn’t retreat. He's pretty sure Mydei's asleep.

…not.

Because he pulls away, and Phainon only has the fleeting thought of feeling like shit before it disintegrates – Mydei pulls him towards his body, locking a muscular arm around Phainon's waist and pushing one leg between the Deliverer's own. With his face buried into Mydei's massive chest, he can barely breathe, and when he does, the scent of melted sugar and spiced cider swirls sharply inside his lungs, inebriating him.

He feels his heartbeats inside his ears. Feels his skin prickle with hot electricity where their bodies converge, feels his bones rattling as he trembles and pulls himself closer, holding Mydei even tighter. Phantom bubbles rise up his ribcage, pushing up his throat and locking it while a hot surge brews behind his eyes. The pressure hurts his skull, so he releases it – takes a shaky breath and allows his walls to come crashing down.

He's lonely, scared, nothing makes any fucking sense, he's angry, so angry he could kill something, so angry he could die. He's frustrated by the lack of communication, he misses the adrenaline of a fight, he misses being useful. He's afraid that he'll stay this way for so long he'll forget what the sky looks like, what music sounds like, how to use his vocal chords.

He's afraid he'll be a burden. That Mydei will get tired. That he'll leave.

He screams into Mydei's chest. Cries in ire and sadness and resentment until his eyes hurt, and until his throat feels sore – until he's so tired that he forgets what he was even upset about.

The only thing left in his silent little world is the cadence of Mydei's heartbeats echoing into his chest, and it easily lulls him to sleep.
